pageCache.text:
About Us
At Finton, children enjoy busy days filled with laughter, friendship and immersive learning experiences. Everyone is included, and strong relationships with parents, governors, guardians, alumni and friends of the School, make it a special community to be part of. Leavers carry their fondness for the School with them long after they leave the classroom and often return as gap year assistants, prospective parents or indeed start their teaching career at Finton.
We value the school’s status as a charitable trust, the benefits of which are many. For children and current parents, it means that the school is well resourced and that fees are kept as low as possible, but for the wider school community, it goes much further than this, embodying the values that underpin everything we do.
Finton House promotes a sense of social responsibility in all its pupils, through its motto “Open Hearts and Guiding Hands” and through its aim that “Everyone feels safe, happy and valued in a community that promotes lifelong health and wellbeing.” This goes well beyond the school gates; and the school continually looks for ways to share its values and resources with the wider community including other schools, youth clubs and nursing homes. Pupils also benefit from a wide range of links with the local community. Charitable work talks from visiting professionals and trips to sites of educational value add to their understanding of the world around them.

pageCache.text:
Headmaster’s Welcome
Happiness is in abundance here. This is largely due to the strong family ethos that makes Finton House so special. We believe in preparing your child to flourish in an ever-changing world, and we do this by giving them a secure, inclusive and happy environment to grow up in – one where every child is able to shine. From their first day at Finton, children are engaged in a range of high-quality learning experiences, developing their self-belief and resilience.
They will move on to their secondary school as confident, caring and compassionate young people with a love of learning. Our highly successful record of entry into first choice schools at 11+, including a high percentage of scholarships and awards in a variety of subjects, speaks for itself: pupils of all ability and interests thrive at Finton House.
Our commitment to pastoral care is as strong as our commitment to providing an outstanding education, both of which underpin our aim of teaching children how to lead a healthy life in its broadest sense. Fun is at the centre of our panning and children learn to exercise their creativity through a wide range of exciting and challenging activities. Look out for the specialist facilities which we have for Science, Computing, Design & Technology, Music and Art, as well as the large sports field where children of all ages can enjoy a range of outdoor activities, games and play sporting fixtures against other schools.
Children have fun here and learn to exercise their creativity through a wide range of exciting and challenging activities. Look out for the specialist facilities which we have for Science, Computing, Design & Technology, Music and Art, as well as the large sports field where children of all ages can enjoy a range of outdoor activities, games and play sporting fixtures against other schools.
Ultimately, the best way to understand why children thrive at Finton House and sense the unique atmosphere is to come and see us for yourself. Please book here and attend an Open Morning.
Ben Freeman, Headmaster

Ethos & Aims
The school motto “Open Hearts and Guiding Hands” sums up the warm and caring relationships that we aim to promote in order to deliver the best education.
Finton House was founded in 1987 as a charitable trust. It has a broad intake in an inclusive environment where children are prepared to thrive in an ever-changing world. Our commitment to pastoral care is as strong as our commitment to providing an outstanding education, and our academic achievements at 11+ speak for themselves.
Values: Self-Belief, Kindness, Respect, Morality, Resilence
At Finton House we live by the Finton Values to ensure that:
These aims are achieved through:
Developing a culture of responsible, caring and happy people
We protect and enhance the wellbeing of the entire Finton community and beyond, by:
Creating a dynamic and diverse learning environment
We offer exciting opportunities for learning by:
Providing a broad, inclusive and inspiring education
We develop the education we provide by:
Ensuring the longevity of Finton House
As a non-profit making charitable trust, we ensure Finton House remains a first–choice school by:
Promoting and embedding diversity across the school.
Providing an exciting, relevant and broad curriculum.
Offering a varied and stimulating extra-curricular programme.
Investing in staffing, facilities and resources.

pageCache.pageTitle: Special Needs Education | Prep School London | Finton House SchoolSpecial Needs Education | Prep School London | Finton House School
pageCache.text:
Special Needs Education
Finton House has a tradition of providing an education for a number of children with known and described special educational needs, providing places are available. The School makes every effort to ensure that reasonable measures are taken to provide accessibility for a range of different special needs.
It should be pointed out that is not always possible to offer places in a year group if it is full. The application process is the same, and places are allocated on a first come, first served basis. Siblings of children, Old Fintonians and children of staff are given priority providing we can meet the child’s needs.
Parents are asked to share, as early as possible, any information about their child’s development on registering which might lead to the need for any additional support at school. The School will request full disclosure of any medical conditions, allergies, learning difficulties and/or disability or emotional/social difficulties. The School will then determine whether the School can meet your child’s needs, using the following criteria:
Depending on the SEND and level of support that is being recommended from the shared reports, we may arrange to observe the child at nursery to ensure we are able to meet the child’s needs once they start at Finton. At that point, if we are able to meet the child’s needs but additional support/resources would be beneficial, we would arrange a meeting or phone call with parents to ensure appropriate support can be put in place for when the child starts.
If it becomes apparent that the School is not able to provide a suitable setting for the child, then the offer of a place will be withdrawn and the deposit will be refunded.
Please contact the Registrar on 020 8682 5757 or email here.

pageCache.text:
History
Finton House Educational Trust was founded in 1987 by Heads Terry O’Neill and Finola Stack. They were generously supported by four families, the Mackenzie-Charringtons, the Macmillans, the Thomsons, and the Nunneleys, who provided financial support and expert advice in setting up the school and moving it from Balham Leisure Centre to its current premises at 171 Trinity Road. The four School Houses are named after them.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bursaries | Independent Prep School | Finton House SchoolBursaries | Independent Prep School | Finton House School
pageCache.text:
Sally Walker Bursary (Y3/4)
Finton House is a registered charity, built on the values of inclusivity, kindness, and philanthropy. These principles have shaped the school’s identity since its foundation and remain central to everything we do.
At the heart of our charitable work is the Sally Walker Fund, named after a much-loved former Headmistress. The Fund supports our outreach efforts and partnerships in areas such as Sport & the Arts, Outdoor Learning, Health & Wellbeing, and the Cost of Living. It also sustains our Bursary Award, which enables children, aged seven or over, who may not otherwise have access to a Finton education, to join our community. These pupils enrich school life with their talents, perspectives, and experiences
Bursary places are based on an academic selection process with an assessment being held at the School as well as a financial screening held by a third party. All cases are judged individually and family circumstances are taken into account. Please fill out a Preliminary Enquiry Form so we can give you an indication of whether a bursary might be available and at what level. All information given will be strictly confidential.
The ideal Bursary applicant will be a child who shows academic aptitude with an outstanding ability in one area of school life, who will benefit fully from the broad curriculum that Finton House offers and will have the ability to go on to further education. The whole family must be committed to supporting their child’s education. Bursaries are available to children aged 7 or over on the 1 September of the year of entry (Year 3 or Year 4).
Applicants seeking an initial indication of eligibility and potential bursary level need to complete the Preliminary Bursary Form. For the formal application, applicants will be asked to provide full supporting documents for the Financial Assessment. All paperwork must be submitted by 31 December in the year prior to entry.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chair’s Review 2025/26 | Finton House SchoolChair’s Review 2025/26 | Finton House School
pageCache.text:
Chair’s Review 2025/26
In my first year as Chair of the Board of Governors, I am delighted to have seen that Finton House School’s core values continue to define our school community and its ethos remains clearly encapsulated in the school motto “Open Hearts and Guiding Hands.”
From its inception the school’s aim has been to educate and develop children of all abilities, including some who need dedicated support. This approach continues to be underlined by the school’s values of self-belief, kindness, respect, morality and resilience.
Thanks to the wisdom and generosity of Finton’s founders, it is constituted as an educational charitable trust. This ensures that all efforts are dedicated towards providing the best possible educational experience for the children in the school’s care. Finton House has no external shareholders – which means that any financial surplus is reinvested back into improving pupils’ learning experience.
Finton House further achieves its charitable aims by actively supporting the local community and offering bursaries to children, who would not otherwise have the opportunity to benefit from a Finton House education. In terms of community engagement over the last 12 months Finton House has supported six charities including Home Start Wandsworth, Little Village, St George’s Hospital Charity, Tom’s Farm, Trinity Fields and Wandsworth Foodbank. In addition to this Finton House shared its facilities with several local schools including, amongst many, Bertrum House, Donhead Preparatory School, Prospect House School, Smallwood Primary School and White House School.
Following the imposition of VAT, increases in National Insurance and general inflationary pressures the Governors are acutely aware of the financial pressure many parents are facing in privately educating their children. We remain resolutely focused on ensuring that Finton House provides the best value for money with the best educational experience.
The 2025/26 academic year has seen Finton House achieve exceptional results across all disciplines. For a school our size and mixed ability, Finton House is punching way above its weight in all areas, competing against much larger schools both locally and nationally. From a Year 6 cohort of 47 pupils, consisting of 24 boys and 23 girls, they achieved a total of 144 offers from leading secondary schools across the UK, averaging three offers per pupil. This year saw a record 39 scholarships, specifically 16 Academic, 13 Sport, 2 Art, 2 Dance, 2 Drama and 1 All-Rounder.
Beyond our graduating class’s successes, the rest of the school also celebrated an extraordinary array of achievements. Notably, Finton House made history, as the only school ever to win both national tournaments at the IFSA Under 11 seven-a-side Football Cup and the EFL Utilita Kids Cup. 20 Finton artists had their work displayed at the Young Art Exhibition at Christie’s, with six pieces ‘Commended’ and one ‘Highly Commended’. The Quiz Club reached the National Quiz Finals and several pupils achieved individual national honours – including at Cambridge University in the Primary Bee Translation and the Poetry By Heart Best in County Award.
Although significant, these extraordinary achievements are a testament to the school’s educational approach. Beyond the academics, Finton House continues to shape character, empower change-makers and nurture the global citizens of tomorrow, guided always by the school’s core values.
Recent marketing analysis and parental survey feedback highlight that word-of-mouth recommendations from past and present families play a vital role in our ongoing success, alongside the dedicated work of Finton’s staff and community. Thanks to their collective effort, the school is entering the 2026/27 year with a full school role for which I and my fellow Governors are deeply grateful.
We are far from resting on our laurels or replying on Finton’s strong reputation. As Governors our focus is to help the continuous building on these strengths to ensure the long-term, sustainable success of Finton House. As always, the success of Finton House rests on the excellence of our teaching and support team led by our Headmaster, Ben Freeman and his Senior Leadership Team who make Finton House what it is today. Their dedication, open mindedness and intellectual curiosity to constantly seek new and better ways to enhance pupils’ development and learning experience is exemplary.
The successful introduction and roll out of the PSB Learning Skills aimed at developing independent enquiry, research, writing and presentation skills, all key lifelong skills, is a wonderful example of this. My fellow Governors and I are extremely fortunate to work with such a dedicated and talented executive team who are the beating heart of the school.
In these challenging times all Governors are acutely aware that global and economic changes are happening all around us. We recently held a strategy day involving the Governors and the Senior Leadership Team which concluded that, whilst not being complacent in the face of numerous challenges facing the private education sector, Finton House does occupy a unique space in the marketplace. We are determined to maintain this for the years ahead so future cohorts of children can continue to enjoy the benefits of a Finton House education.
I am extremely fortunate and humbled to have been appointed Chair of Governors. To be able to support and help to guide such a unique and special school continues to be a great privilege. My own children attended Finton House over 25 years ago and to find that the founding ethos of the school has remained unchanged and is as relevant today as it was in 1987 is a testament to all my predecessors and the founder’s foresight. As Governors we are determined to maintain Finton House’s unique character, spirit and values in the years ahead.
James Vickers Chair of Governors

Clubs & Wraparound Care
Our extra-curricular clubs provide an exciting enrichment of the children’s experience at Finton and cover a huge range of activities such as art, cookery, sports, drama, film, jewellery making, cheerleading and much more. These optional clubs offer the children a vast range of different opportunities and act as extensions to the school day (8.30am – 4.00pm). After school clubs are typically an hour long (4.00 – 5.00pm Mon – Thu and 3.30 – 4.30pm on Fri), with some running longer if they are off-site.
Off-site clubs include Tom’s Farm Club, Swimming Squad, Hockey Club and Grandfriends Club.
In addition to this, we offer wraparound care in the form of Larks (before school care) and Owls/Owlets (after school care). Children can be dropped off at 8.00am for Larks and can remain in Owls/Owlets after school until 6.00pm (5.30pm on Fridays).

Act Drama
Act Drama
‘Pretend to be an animal starting with the letter B!’ Children in the Act Drama Club are encouraged to let their imagination run wild in interactive activities and role plays which foster creativity, build self-esteem and develop the children’s oral communication skills.

Chess

Playing chess is not only a great exercise for the brain, but it also puts the children’s patience and discipline to the test!

pageCache.text:
Residential Trips Round Up 2025
We had an exciting couple of weeks as Years 3, 4, 5 and 6 all headed off on their residential trips. 2025 At Finton, we place great value on the importance of pupils stepping beyond the classroom to explore new environments, meet new people, and develop real-world skills. Each academic year, we offer a wide array of enriching trips that support and enhance our curriculum. Being located in the heart of London, we are incredibly fortunate to have world-class cultural and educational experiences right on our doorstep. Our pupils regularly visit iconic landmarks such as the London Eye, museums, galleries, and theatres; becoming true experts in their local city.
As part of our commitment to a diverse education, we also offer visits to places of worship including churches, temples, mosques and synagogues, giving pupils the opportunity to learn about different faiths and cultures.
A highlight of the school year are the residential trips offered to years 3 to 6, giving pupils the chance to travel further afield to places like Wales, Dorset, and even France in Year 6. These unforgettable experiences include kayaking, fishing, white-water rafting, orienteering, and archery, helping pupils to build independence, teamwork, and a sense of adventure.
All in all, residentials are an incredibly valuable experience for our pupils and so much learning takes place which cannot be recreated in the classroom. A huge thank you goes to all of the staff who attended and to the pupils for representing Finton so admirably.
